branches.label: WHO IS TAXED, AND ON WHAT
leaves: EMPLOYEES and company directors, on salary, bonuses and taxable benefits in kind such as a car or private medical insurance
SOLE TRADERS and PARTNERS in any kind of partnership, on taxable trading profits whether or not the profits are withdrawn
SHAREHOLDERS on dividends, and LENDERS and DEBENTURE HOLDERS on the interest they receive
OWNERS OF RENTAL PROPERTY on property income, and savers on bank and bond interest
EXEMPT: many social security benefits, tax credits, interest on national savings certificates and income from an ISA
The tax year runs from 6 April to 5 April

branches.label: THE CALCULATION, IN ORDER
leaves: TOTAL income is every gross non-exempt source added together

NET income is total income less personal pension contributions and interest on QUALIFYING LOANS, meaning loans to make capital contributions to an unincorporated business or to buy shares in a company
TAXABLE income is net income less the personal allowance
The three types are taxed in a fixed ORDER: non-savings first, then savings, then dividends as the top slice
Add the tax on each type together, then deduct tax already paid at source such as PAYE

branches.label: TRADING PROFITS, CAPITAL ALLOWANCES AND LOSSES
leaves: Deductible expenses must be INCOME related rather than capital, and incurred WHOLLY AND EXCLUSIVELY for the business
A dual-purpose expense is deductible as to the business proportion, provided the business and non-business parts can be separated
Capital allowances are a form of tax-approved depreciation, deducted as an expense in arriving at taxable trading profits
Each partner is taxed on their own share, set by the agreement or equally if there is none, and the partnership itself pays no income tax
The agreement can give a partner a preferential allocation as salary or interest on capital before the balance is shared
A trading LOSS is never relieved automatically: the taxpayer must claim, and the decision tree below picks the relief

branches.label: PAYING, AND ANTI-AVOIDANCE
leaves: Employees have tax deducted at source under PAYE, using a tax code HMRC sends to the employer
Anyone whose tax is not all deducted at source must SELF-ASSESS, filing online by 31 January after the tax year, or on paper by 31 October
Payments on account fall due on 31 January in the tax year and 31 July after it, each 50% of last year's liability, with a balancing payment on 31 January
TAX PLANNING is lawful, TAX EVASION is illegal, and TAX AVOIDANCE is lawful but artificial and done only to pay less tax
The GENERAL ANTI-ABUSE RULE lets HMRC set aside an arrangement that cannot reasonably be regarded as a reasonable course of action

visuals.label: Decision tree - which loss relief is available for this trading loss?

nodes.q: 1. Is the loss in one of the first four tax years of the trade?

a.v: EARLY TRADE LOSSES RELIEF carries the loss back against the net income of the three preceding tax years, taking the EARLIEST year first.
Go to question 2.

nodes.q: 2. Has the trader ceased trading?

a.v: TERMINAL LOSS RELIEF deducts the loss from trading profits in the tax year of cessation, then carries it back three years taking the LATEST year first.
Go to question 3.

nodes.q: 3. Has the business been transferred to a company in return for shares?

a.v: Unused losses stay with the trader and are set against salary or dividends from the company for any year the shares are held.
Go to question 4.

nodes.q: 4. Is there income now to absorb the loss?

a.v: Set the loss against net income of the current tax year or the previous one, and the taxpayer chooses which to take first.
Carry the loss forward against future profits of the SAME trade. This is a last resort because it delays the relief.

nodes.q: 5. Any loss still unrelieved?

a.v: The balance can be used as an allowable loss to reduce capital gains and so save capital gains tax.
A claim must use all the loss available or absorb all the available income, so the personal allowance can be wasted.

visuals.label: The eight steps of an income tax calculation
data: Calculate TOTAL income, meaning every source of gross non-exempt income including non-savings, savings and dividend income.
Calculate NET income, being total income less allowable deductions for interest on qualifying loans and for personal pension contributions.
Calculate TAXABLE income, being net income less the personal allowance where one is available.
Split taxable income into its three types: non-savings, savings and dividend income.
Consider the reliefs available, chiefly the personal savings allowance and the dividend allowance.
Apply the tax rates to each type in the fixed order of non-savings income, then savings income, then dividend income.
Add the amounts calculated for each type together to give the total tax liability.
Deduct tax already paid at source, such as under PAYE, to show how much tax is still due.

Income from pensions

branches.label: HOW IT WORKS IN PRACTICE
leaves: The Senedd has set a proportion of income tax since 6 April 2019, by resolution before each tax year on the Welsh government's proposal

notes.head: 7.16.2 Basis of charge and the chargeable persons
body: The overview map names who is taxed and on what. These are the points the map does not carry.

Do NOT try to memorise the rates. The manual says explicitly that rates, allowances and bands will be supplied in the assessment. Concentrate on who is taxed, what is taxed, and whether there is a lawful way to reduce the bill.
Rates, allowances and reliefs normally change in April each year, to coincide with the start of the tax year.
Sole traders and partners are taxed on the profits of a trade or profession whether or not the profits are actually drawn out of the business.
In a partnership each partner is taxed on their total share of the partnership income. The share follows the partnership agreement, or is equal if there is no agreement.
The agreement may give one or more partners a PREFERENTIAL allocation, categorised as salary or as interest on capital, with the balance then shared in the agreed proportions.

Worked example: on profits of £205,000 where Rod takes a salary of £20,000 and Jane £5,000 as interest, the residual £180,000 splits equally at £60,000 each. Rod is taxed on £80,000, Jane on £65,000 and Freddy on £60,000.
The partnership itself is not liable to income tax. Each partner is individually liable for their own tax and not for their partners'.
The WHOLLY AND EXCLUSIVELY test is applied strictly. Where an expense is materially for a personal or non-business purpose, HMRC disallows it entirely rather than apportioning it.
CURRENCY: the writing-down allowance for main pool assets has been reduced from 18% to 14%, which also affects capital allowances for corporation tax at 7.17.2.3.

notes.head: 7.16.3 Calculating the tax, and the Enterprise Investment Scheme
body: The eight steps are in the steps panel above, and the order in which income is taxed is in the grid above.
If the personal allowance exceeds net income the excess cannot be carried forward to another tax year, because the allowance is annual only. The taxpayer simply pays no income tax that year.
Spouses and civil partners each have their own personal allowance.

body.head: The three conditions for the marriage allowance
items: The couple are married or in a civil partnership.
The transferring spouse or civil partner has income of less than the personal allowance.
The recipient spouse or civil partner is a basic rate taxpayer.

body: The transferor's personal allowance is reduced by the amount transferred, but the recipient does not simply add it to their own allowance. Instead the recipient's tax liability is reduced by an amount equal to 20% of the transferred allowance.
Income tax is PROGRESSIVE: the higher the taxable income, the higher the rate on the top slice.
ENTERPRISE INVESTMENT SCHEME: a taxpayer who subscribes for new shares in a qualifying unquoted trading company may deduct 30% of the value of the shares from their income tax liability.
The deduction can be taken for the tax year of purchase or for the previous one, and split between the two years in any proportion.
The annual ceiling is £1m of subscriptions, giving relief of up to £300,000, rising to £2m and £600,000 for a knowledge-intensive company.
The taxpayer must not be CONNECTED with the company: they must not own more than 30% of the ordinary shares, and must not be an employee or an associate of one.
Relief cannot create a negative income tax figure, so it cannot generate a repayment, though it can be set against a liability in the previous tax year.

notes.head: 7.16.4 Payment, collection and trading losses
body: Employees and company directors have tax deducted from their pay under PAYE and paid over to HMRC, which is deduction at source. HMRC sends the employer a tax code showing the tax-free allowance and rate for that employee.
PAYE is not always accurate, so some employees still have to file a return, and any tax deducted under PAYE is then offset against the liability for the year.

Sole traders and partners are taxed on the profits made during the TAX year, whatever accounting year they have chosen. Where the accounting year differs, profits from two accounting years must be apportioned.

Apportionment is normally by days, remembering 366 days in a leap year, though another reasonable method such as months or weeks may be used. Where the profits are not yet known, a provisional estimate goes in the return and is amended later.
Most self-employed people and landlords will increasingly have to submit quarterly updates to HMRC of income and expenses drawn from their digital records.

body.head: When payments on account are required
items: The taxpayer is self-employed with a tax bill of £1,000 or more, or has had 80% or less of their tax deducted at source.
The first payment on account falls due on 31 January in the tax year in question.
The second falls due on 31 July after the end of the tax year.
Each payment on account is 50% of the previous year's liability after credit for tax deducted at source, and any balancing payment is due on 31 January with the return.

body: Penalties are payable for a late return, and for late or non-payment of balancing payments. Some penalties are behaviour related, turning on whether an error was careless or deliberate.

The loss relief decision tree above works through the options. Two points bind them all: relief is not automatic and must be claimed, and no partial claims are allowed, so a claim must use all of the loss or absorb all of the available income.

Worked example of the current year rule: a trading loss of £40,000 against rental income of £27,000 absorbs the whole £27,000 even though the personal allowance would otherwise have covered part of it, leaving £13,000 to carry back to the previous year.

Worked example of the spill-over into gains: a trading loss of £30,000 set against property income of £25,000 leaves £5,000, which can reduce capital gains of £18,000 down to £13,000, before the annual exemption is applied.

notes.head: 7.16.5 to 7.16.6 Anti-avoidance
body: The grid above separates planning, avoidance and evasion. Parliament attacks avoidance on two fronts.
The FIRST is specific provision in the tax legislation, spelling out precisely which transactions are unacceptable and what follows. Some of these are called targeted anti-avoidance rules.
The SECOND is the GENERAL ANTI-ABUSE RULE, an overriding rule covering income tax, capital gains tax, corporation tax, inheritance tax and others.
It sits above the specific legislation, so it can be used even where an abusive arrangement exploits a targeted anti-avoidance rule.

The DOUBLE REASONABLENESS TEST is the threshold. HMRC may set an arrangement aside only if it can prove the arrangement cannot reasonably be regarded as a reasonable course of action, which is a high bar to clear.
HMRC must obtain the opinion of an INDEPENDENT ADVISORY PANEL on the reasonableness of the arrangement before treating it as abusive.

The remedy is a just and reasonable tax adjustment, such as taxing the income in a legitimate way. The rule itself carries no separate penalty, but a taxpayer in an abusive scheme can be penalised under the general tax laws for filing an inaccurate return.

An ENABLER, meaning someone who in the course of their business enables an abusive arrangement, can be made to pay a penalty equal to the value of the benefit they received for facilitating it. There is a right of appeal to a tax tribunal.

EIS ANTI-AVOIDANCE: the shares must be held for at least 3 years, and disposal within 3 years of issue claws the relief back, unless the taxpayer dies or gifts the shares to a spouse or civil partner.
Claw-back also follows if the scheme conditions cease to be met, for instance because the taxpayer becomes an employee or acquires more than 30% of the ordinary share capital.
SETTLEMENT RULES: a parent cannot shift income to a minor unmarried child to use the child's personal allowance or lower rates of tax.

Where a parent's gift produces more than £100 of income in a tax year, the whole of the income arising from that gift is taxed as the parent's. Gifts to minor grandchildren, nieces, nephews or friends are not caught.

notes.head: 7.16.7 Welsh income tax
body: The Welsh income tax map above carries the substance. Two points are worth stating separately.
The mechanism is subtraction and addition: the UK income tax rate is reduced by a specified percentage, and the Welsh rate of income tax is then paid on top of that reduced UK rate.
Where a taxpayer has residences in more than one part of the UK, the days spent in each of England, Scotland and Northern Ireland are counted SEPARATELY when testing which connection is closest.

statutes.text: Sets out the step-by-step calculation of an individual's income tax liability, from total income through net income and taxable income to the tax due. The 2026 BUS7 chapter presents the same sequence as eight steps without citing the section.
Provides for the basic, higher and additional rates of income tax. The actual percentages and band limits are set annually and will be supplied in the assessment.

statutes.ref: Government of Wales Act 2006 (as amended by the Wales Act 2014)
statutes.text: Gives the Senedd power, exercised since 6 April 2019, to set a proportion of the income tax paid by Welsh taxpayers on non-savings and non-dividend income, by resolution before each tax year.

An overriding rule covering income tax, capital gains tax, corporation tax and inheritance tax. HMRC may set aside abusive tax arrangements only where it proves they cannot reasonably be regarded as a reasonable course of action, after obtaining the opinion of an independent advisory panel. The remedy is a just and reasonable tax adjustment, and an enabler can be penalised to the value of the benefit received.

Anti-avoidance provision preventing a parent from shifting income to a minor unmarried child. Income of more than £100 a year arising from a parent's gift is taxed as the parent's income. Gifts to minor grandchildren, nieces, nephews or friends are outside the rule.

7.16.tip: ⚡ 7.16 spine. You are not asked to memorise the figures, only the machinery. Work the calculation in order: total income, then net income, then taxable income after the personal allowance, then split it into non-savings, savings and dividends and tax them in that order, with dividends always the top slice. The personal allowance tapers away above £100,000. A trading deduction must be INCOME rather than capital, and wholly and exclusively for the business. Losses need a claim and allow no partial claims. Planning is lawful, avoidance is lawful but artificial, and evasion is a crime.

7.17.title: Corporation Tax

visuals.label: Mind map — the whole of 7.17

branches.label: WHO PAYS, ON WHAT, AND FOR WHICH PERIOD
leaves: Companies pay corporation tax on their TAXABLE PROFITS for their accounting period, at the rate applicable to the relevant financial years
Taxable profits are made up of three things: TRADING INCOME PROFITS, NON-TRADING INCOME PROFITS and CAPITAL GAINS
The FINANCIAL YEAR runs 1 April to 31 March; the ACCOUNTING PERIOD is the company's own elected period, and it is on that period that it pays
Before the total profit is taxed the company may deduct any payments made to NATIONAL CHARITIES
Companies pay corporation tax on their chargeable gains — there is no capital gains tax on a company

branches.label: STEP 1 — INCOME PROFITS
leaves: Start with TURNOVER, then deduct legitimate expenses (the cost of sales) and capital allowances
An expense is deductible only if it is WHOLLY AND EXCLUSIVELY for the purposes of the business, is NOT PROHIBITED BY STATUTE, and is of an INCOME NATURE with an element of regularity
Business entertainment, doubtful debt provisions and depreciation are NOT deductible
Add other non-trading income such as RENT RECEIPTS and INTEREST; DIVIDENDS received from another company are usually exempt and do not count
Dividends the company PAYS are not an allowable expense — they come out of post-tax profits

branches.label: CAPITAL ALLOWANCES ARE TAX-APPROVED DEPRECIATION
leaves: 100% FIRST-YEAR ALLOWANCE for environmentally friendly items such as energy-efficient heating, water-saving machinery, charging points and zero-emission vehicles
100% FULL EXPENSING and 50% first-year allowances for other plant and machinery, uncapped but available only for NEW, not second-hand or refurbished, machinery
ANNUAL INVESTMENT ALLOWANCE gives a 100% deduction on plant and machinery excluding cars, up to £1m; it cannot be carried forward and a new allowance arises each accounting period
A first-year allowance cannot be claimed IN ADDITION to the AIA on the same expenditure — where both are available the company chooses
WRITING-DOWN ALLOWANCES on a reducing balance: 14% a year for the main pool, 6% a year for the special rate pool of long-life assets, integral features and some cars

branches.label: STEP 2 — CHARGEABLE GAINS
leaves: Take the proceeds of sale, or market value, and deduct the acquisition cost and the costs of acquisition such as legal fees
Then deduct ENHANCEMENT EXPENDITURE reflected in the value of the asset on disposal, and the INCIDENTAL COSTS OF DISPOSAL
INDEXATION ALLOWANCE is available only for assets owned before 1 January 2018 and has been FROZEN from that date
BUSINESS ASSETS ROLL-OVER RELIEF defers the gain where the proceeds are reinvested in other qualifying assets, between 1 YEAR BEFORE and 3 YEARS AFTER the sale
CAPITAL LOSSES can only be set against capital gains, in the current year or carried forward — never carried back, and never against income

branches.label: CLOSE COMPANIES AND ANTI-AVOIDANCE
leaves: A CLOSE COMPANY is UK-resident and controlled by FIVE OR FEWER PARTICIPATORS, or by any number of participators who are also DIRECTORS
A loan to a participator makes the company pay HMRC tax at the HIGHER DIVIDEND RATE, refunded when the loan is repaid or written off — a pure cash-flow cost
A cheap or interest-free loan to an EMPLOYEE creates a taxable benefit measured by the official rate of interest
TRANSFER PRICING: a transaction between group companies not at arm's length that produces a tax advantage is adjusted to the arm's-length outcome
CHANGE OF OWNERSHIP: carried-forward trading losses are blocked where HMRC considers there has been a major change in the nature or conduct of the trade after the acquisition

visuals.label: Decision tree — which rate, and what can be done with a loss?

nodes.q: 1. What are the company's total taxable profits for the accounting period?

a.v: The small profits rate of 19% applies to the whole of the taxable profit.
The main rate of 25% applies to the whole of the taxable profit.

The main rate of 25% applies but can be reduced by claiming marginal relief, which gives a gradual increase in the effective rate from 19% up to 25%. The marginal effective rate on the band itself is 26.5%.

nodes.q: 2. The company has made a TRADING loss. What can it do with it?

a.k: SET IT AGAINST TOTAL PROFITS OF THE CURRENT PERIOD
a.v: Against all profits of the period, income and capital alike, if there are any.
Against total profits of the preceding 12 months, but only AFTER a current-period offset has been made.
Against total profits of a later accounting period, with no time limit.

nodes.q: 3. The loss is a CAPITAL loss instead. Does the same apply?

a.v: A capital loss can only be offset against chargeable gains. It can never be used against income profits.
It can be set against gains in the current tax year and carried forward against future gains, but it can never be carried back.

nodes.q: 4. When is the tax due?

a.k: 9 MONTHS AND 1 DAY AFTER THE END OF THE ACCOUNTING PERIOD
a.v: That is the normal rule for payment.

a.k: 12 MONTHS AFTER THE END OF THE PERIOD
a.v: That is the deadline for the corporation tax RETURN, not the payment.
Companies or groups with larger profits must pay in instalments rather than under the normal rule. Underpaid or overdue tax attracts interest and penalties.

visuals.label: Steps — the five steps of a corporation tax calculation, in order
data: Identify income profits: turnover, less expenditure wholly and exclusively incurred for the purposes of the business, less capital allowances, plus other income such as rent and interest but not dividends received, less trading losses.

Identify capital profits: disposal value, less (indexed) allowable expenditure such as the acquisition cost, considering business assets roll-over relief to postpone the gain, less capital and trading losses.
Cumulate the income profits and the capital profits, unless the gain has been rolled over.
Deduct any qualifying payments to charity.
Apply the appropriate rate or rates to the resulting taxable profits, according to the size of the company.

rows: Which companies
Close companies only. The rule exists because there is normally no tax on a loan, so a participator could take value out untaxed.

Allowable deductions against taxable trading profits, as are employers' National Insurance contributions.
Taxed as employment income and subject to National Insurance.

Other recognised methods of extracting profit.
Because dividend rates are lower than the rates for non-savings and savings income, owner-directors typically take a small salary and the majority of their remuneration as dividends.

notes.head: 7.17.2 Basis of charge
body: Two periods matter. The financial year runs from 1 April to 31 March annually. The company's accounting period is its own elected or chosen period, and it is on that period annually that the company pays corporation tax.
Companies are charged corporation tax on their taxable profits for the accounting period, at the rate applicable to the relevant financial years.
Taxable profits comprise trading income profits, non-trading income profits and capital gains.
These are cumulated to give total profit, but before that total is taxed the company may deduct any payments made to national charities.
The current financial year is 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027, FY 2026/2027, and all the corporation tax rates are the same as for FY 2025/2026.

notes.head: 7.17.2.1 Step 1 — income receipts
body: Trading income is usually where most company income comes from. The calculation of trading profits for companies, sole traders and partnerships is broadly similar: from turnover the company deducts legitimate expenses, sometimes called its cost of sales, and capital allowances.
A company also pays corporation tax on non-trading income, for example rent receipts and interest income, which is added to its taxable trading income.
Dividend income received as a shareholder in another company is usually exempt and so does not count towards taxable income.
To be deductible, expenditure must be wholly and exclusively incurred for the purpose of the business. Raw materials for production qualify; most business entertainment costs do not.
It must not be prohibited by statute, which rules out a doubtful debt provision and depreciation.
It must be of an income nature, with an element of regularity, such as rent or wages paid to employees or directors.
Dividends a company pays to its shareholders are not an allowable trading expense; they are paid from post-tax profits.
Capital allowances are a form of tax-approved depreciation for certain capital expenditure, deducted from trading profits as though they were an expense. They exist to encourage investment.

body.head: The manual's worked example
items: Newco has turnover of £1,300,000. It deducts stock purchases of £580,000, salaries of £120,000 and utilities of £20,000, reducing taxable profits to £580,000.
Its business entertainment costs of £5,000 are not deductible and must be paid out of taxed profits.
It deducts a first-year allowance of £160,000 for qualifying green plant and machinery, reducing taxable profits to £420,000.

body: Structures and buildings allowances also exist for buildings and other structures used by a business, but the detail is outside the scope of the manual.

notes.head: 7.17.2.2 Trading loss relief
body: A trading loss can be set against total profits of the current accounting period, if there are any other profits, whether income or capital.
It can be carried back and set against total profits of the preceding 12 months, but only after a current-period offset has been made.
It can be carried forward and set against total profits of a later accounting period.

The manual's example: Hogg Foods Ltd has a trading loss of £85,000, chargeable gains of £20,000 and property income of £17,000. The loss is offset against all profits of £37,000 for the year, leaving £48,000, which can then be carried back 12 months or carried forward.

notes.head: 7.17.2.3 Step 2 — taxable chargeable gains
body: A corporate gain arises where an asset increases in value while the company owns it. Companies pay corporation tax on chargeable gains, not capital gains tax.
First take the proceeds of sale, or the market value, and deduct the original acquisition cost together with any associated expenditure incurred on acquisition, such as legal fees.

Then deduct enhancement expenditure reflected in the value of the asset on disposal, for example an extension to a building, and the incidental costs of disposal such as legal, surveyor or auctioneer fees.

For assets owned before 1 January 2018 an indexation allowance gives a further deduction for inflationary increases. It has been frozen from that date, so assets acquired afterwards get nothing. The calculation itself is outside the scope of the manual.

Business assets roll-over relief lets a company defer a chargeable gain, and so the tax on it, where it disposes of a qualifying business asset. Qualifying assets include land, buildings and plant and machinery, but NOT shares.

Two conditions apply to the relief: the proceeds of sale must be reinvested in other qualifying assets, which need not be the same kind, and the business must have been trading both when the old assets were sold and when the new ones were bought.
The reinvestment must be made within 1 year before or 3 years after the asset is sold. The charge is deferred until the new asset is disposed of and no new qualifying assets are purchased.

Capital losses can only be offset against chargeable gains, never against income profits. They can be used against gains in the current tax year and carried forward against future gains, but they cannot be carried back.

notes.head: 7.17.2.4 Steps 3 to 5 — calculation, payment and collection
body: Once taxable income profits and taxable chargeable gains, less losses, have been calculated for the accounting period, they are added together.
Any qualifying payments to charity are then deducted from the total profit.
The relevant corporation tax rate is applied to the taxable profit. The rate depends on whether the company qualifies as a small company.
Corporation tax is due 9 months and 1 day after the end of the accounting period. The corporation tax return for the same period is due 12 months after the end of the period.
Any corporation tax underpaid or overdue is subject to interest and penalties.
Companies or groups of companies with larger profits must pay earlier than the normal rule, in quarterly instalments.

Where a company has one or more associated companies, meaning companies under common control, the £50,000 and £250,000 thresholds are divided by the number of associated companies, so a company with one associated company divides them by two.

notes.head: 7.17.3 Company distributions and other extraction of profits
body: The taxation of distributions is designed to ensure that any value given to a shareholder that they have not paid for through full consideration is taxed as a dividend, that is, as income received by the shareholder.
Dividends are not tax-deductible as an expense for the company and are paid from distributable profits, meaning profits after tax.

A distribution in specie, also called a dividend in kind, arises from a sale, transfer or other disposition by a company of a non-cash asset, for example a transfer of property or machinery to a shareholder instead of a cash dividend.
Dividends received by a shareholder are chargeable to income tax in England and Wales at the shareholder's marginal rate, after any non-savings and savings income has been taxed.
Dividends are not earnings for National Insurance purposes, so no National Insurance contributions are due, even where the shareholder is also an employee or director of the company.

That is why owner-directors of smaller companies typically pay themselves a small salary and extract the majority of their remuneration as dividends: dividend tax rates are lower than the rates for non-savings and savings income.

Salary, bonuses and other benefits in kind paid to directors and employees are allowable deductions against the taxable trading profits of the company, as are employers' National Insurance contributions.

Profits can also be extracted through company pension contributions, rent paid for the use of a building owned by a shareholder-director, or interest on a loan made to the company by a shareholder-director.

notes.head: 7.17.4 Close companies
body: A close company is a company resident in the UK which is controlled by five or fewer participators, or by any number of participators who are also directors, including shadow directors.
A participator is a shareholder or a person with the right to acquire shares.
Control means ownership of more than 50% of the shares, more than half of the voting power, or the right to acquire over 50% of the shares.

notes.head: 7.17.5 Anti-avoidance provisions
body: HMRC is aware that companies, especially those controlled by a limited number of individuals, can be used to get profits into the hands of those individuals without tax being paid, in particular by loans that are interest-free or later written off.
The loans-to-participators rule applies only to close companies. See the grid above for the charge, the timing, the refund and the two escapes.

Separately, where a company makes a loan to an employee, who may also be a shareholder, a taxable benefit arises if no interest is charged, or if interest is charged below the official rate of interest on beneficial loans set by HMRC. The official rate is currently 3.75%.

The manual's example: Henry borrows £80,000 from his own company, of which he is the sole director and employee and one of four shareholders, and pays no interest. He is deemed to receive a benefit of £80,000 at the official rate, on which he pays income tax, and the company pays National Insurance on the value of that benefit. Because Henry is also a participator in a close company, the close company rules apply as well.

Transfer pricing: where goods or services pass between group companies, prices could be set so that the profit lands in the company with the lowest corporation tax rate, if the companies are in different countries, or with the most brought-forward losses, if they are both in the UK.

Where a transaction is found not to be at arm's length and a tax advantage results from it, anti-avoidance legislation adjusts the outcome to what would have happened on an arm's-length basis, removing the advantage.
Change of ownership: rules prevent a company carrying forward its trading losses where ownership has changed and the new owner acquired the company only in order to use those losses.
If HMRC considers that a major change in the nature or conduct of the trade or business has taken place after the acquisition, it will stop the carried-forward losses from being used.

statutes.text: The main charging statute for corporation tax on the income profits of companies, including the rules on trading income, non-trading income and deductible expenditure.
Carries the rates of corporation tax, the small profits rate and marginal relief, the associated companies rules, trading loss relief, and the close company rules including loans to participators.
Governs the computation of chargeable gains, allowable expenditure, indexation allowance for assets held before 1 January 2018, business assets roll-over relief and the treatment of capital losses.
Governs capital allowances: first-year allowances, full expensing, the annual investment allowance, and writing-down allowances on the main pool and the special rate pool.

statutes.ref: Income Tax (Trading and Other Income) Act 2005
statutes.text: Charges dividends and other distributions received by an individual shareholder to income tax, at the dividend rates and after non-savings and savings income.
Contains the transfer pricing rules, which substitute the arm's-length result where a transaction between connected parties produces a tax advantage.

7.17.tip: ⚡ 7.17 SPINE — five steps in order: income profits, capital gains, cumulate, deduct charitable payments, apply the rate. Dividends RECEIVED are exempt and dividends PAID are not deductible. Take the capital allowances before the rate — the annual investment allowance, full expensing for NEW machinery only, then writing down on the reducing balance. Split the losses, because they behave differently: a TRADING loss goes against total profits, back twelve months or forward indefinitely, while a CAPITAL loss goes against gains only and can NEVER go back. Pay nine months and a day after the accounting period ends and file at twelve months. Finish by asking whether it is a CLOSE company, because a loan to a participator carries its own charge.

7.18.title: Capital Gains Tax

visuals.label: Mind map — the whole of 7.18

branches.label: WHEN THE CHARGE ARISES
leaves: A CHARGEABLE PERSON: an individual, a trustee or a personal representative
A CHARGEABLE DISPOSAL: a sale, a gift, a disposal of part, or the loss or destruction of the asset
A CHARGEABLE ASSET: most commonly land, buildings, goodwill or an interest in a business, and shares
A company making a gain pays CORPORATION TAX on it, not capital gains tax
A UK resident is charged on worldwide assets; a non-resident only on disposals of interests in UK land, residential or commercial

branches.label: WHAT ESCAPES THE CHARGE ALTOGETHER
leaves: The taxpayer's MAIN RESIDENCE, through private residence relief
PRIVATE CARS, including classic and vintage models
Gains made inside an INDIVIDUAL SAVINGS ACCOUNT
WASTING CHATTELS — tangible moveable property with a predictable life of 50 years or less
GOVERNMENT BONDS, and a non-wasting chattel sold for £6,000 or less
DEATH is not an occasion of charge: the beneficiary inherits at probate value, the market value at the date of death
Transfers between SPOUSES or CIVIL PARTNERS pass on a no-gain, no-loss basis, and gifts to registered charities are normally exempt

branches.label: CALCULATING THE GAIN
leaves: Start with the CONSIDERATION actually received on a sale at arm's length
Use MARKET VALUE instead where the disposal is a gift or is made to a connected person
A BAD BARGAIN made at arm's length is taken at the actual price, because there may be a sound commercial reason for it
Deduct the ACQUISITION COST and expenses — the purchase price or market value on acquisition, legal fees and stamp duty land tax
Deduct INCIDENTAL COSTS OF DISPOSAL such as legal fees, valuation fees and advertising
Deduct ENHANCEMENT EXPENDITURE, but only if it is still reflected in the asset at the date of disposal

branches.label: THE SIX RELIEFS
leaves: BUSINESS ASSET DISPOSAL RELIEF taxes qualifying gains at a lower rate, up to a lifetime limit
GIFT HOLD-OVER RELIEF lets the donor give a business asset away and passes the gain to the donee
BUSINESS ASSETS ROLL-OVER RELIEF defers the gain where the proceeds are reinvested in new qualifying assets
INCORPORATION RELIEF defers the gain when a business is transferred to a company in exchange for shares
ENTERPRISE INVESTMENT SCHEME RELIEF defers a gain of any kind that is reinvested in qualifying unquoted shares
PRIVATE RESIDENCE RELIEF exempts the gain on the taxpayer's home, wholly or in part

branches.label: LOSSES, ALLOWANCE, RATE AND PAYMENT
leaves: Losses of the same tax year MUST be set against that year's gains, automatically
Unused losses are carried forward INDEFINITELY, but the annual exempt amount can never be carried forward
Both losses and the annual exempt amount should be aimed at the gains taxed at the HIGHER rate
The rate turns on the taxpayer's INCOME: gains within the unused basic rate band are taxed at the lower rate
Capital gains tax is payable on 31 JANUARY after the tax year, with no payments on account
A disposal of UK RESIDENTIAL PROPERTY must be reported and paid within 60 DAYS of completion

visuals.label: Decision tree — which relief is this question about?

nodes.q: 1. The taxpayer is GIVING the asset away

a.v: Donor and donee elect jointly. The donor's gain is not taxed now; instead the donee's acquisition cost is reduced by that gain, so the donee pays on both gains when they eventually dispose of it.

Assets used in a trade or profession carried on by the transferor or by their personal company, meaning a holding of at least 5% of the voting rights; shares in an unquoted trading company; shares in the transferor's personal company; and assets qualifying for agricultural property relief.

a.k: IF THE DONEE IS A SPOUSE
a.v: No relief is needed — the transfer is automatically no-gain, no-loss, and the recipient takes the donor's original cost.

nodes.q: 2. The taxpayer is SELLING and buying something else

a.v: Available to a sole trader or partner who reinvests the proceeds in other qualifying business assets. Qualifying assets include land, buildings and plant and machinery, but NOT shares.
The reinvestment must be made within 1 year before, or 3 years after, the sale of the old asset. The business must have been trading both when the old asset was sold and when the new one was bought.

Full relief only if ALL the proceeds are reinvested. Partial relief where only part is reinvested, where the old asset was only partly used in the business, or where the replacement is a depreciating asset.

The gain can be on ANY type of asset, not just a business asset. Invest it in shares in an EIS qualifying unquoted trading company, up to 1 year before or 3 years after the gain, and the tax on the amount invested is deferred until the EIS shares are sold.

nodes.q: 3. The taxpayer is selling or giving away the BUSINESS ITSELF

a.v: A lower rate on qualifying gains, up to a lifetime limit of £1m of gains for each individual.

All or part of a trading business carried on as a sole trader or in partnership for at least 2 years; shares in a trading company where the individual owns at least 5% of the ordinary voting shares AND was an officer or employee for 2 years; and assets owned by the individual and used by the trading business in the 2 years before disposal. Selling one asset on its own does not qualify unless it falls within those provisions.

A different relief. Where an individual transfers their business or partnership interest as a going concern to a company and takes shares in exchange, the gain is deferred by reducing the acquisition cost of those shares.

nodes.q: 4. The asset is the taxpayer's HOME

a.v: If the taxpayer lived there as their home throughout their ownership, 100% of the gain is exempt. The relief covers land or garden of up to half a hectare, and more in some cases.
Exempt gain = gain × (period of occupation ÷ period of ownership). Only absence during ownership can make any part of the gain chargeable.

a.k: THE LAST 9 MONTHS ARE ALWAYS OCCUPATION
a.v: The taxpayer is deemed to be living there for the final 9 months of ownership whether they were or not, provided only that they occupied it as their home at some time.

Each must be sandwiched between periods of actual occupation: absence abroad by reason of employment, which is unlimited; absence working elsewhere, employed or self-employed, up to 4 years; and absence for ANY reason at all, up to 3 years. They can be added together.

visuals.label: The six steps of a capital gains tax calculation, in order
data: Identify a chargeable asset that is the subject of a chargeable disposal by a chargeable person
Calculate the gain: consideration, actual or deemed, less allowable deductions such as acquisition costs and other permitted expenditure

Consider the deferral and exemption reliefs — roll-over, hold-over, incorporation, EIS and private residence relief. Business asset disposal relief is NOT applied here; it is a rate, applied at step 6
Deduct any allowable losses, aiming them at the gains that will be taxed at the higher rate
Deduct the annual exempt amount, again aiming it at the gains that will be taxed at the higher rate
Calculate the tax, checking first whether the taxpayer is a basic or higher rate income taxpayer, and applying the business asset disposal relief rate to qualifying assets

visuals.label: The figures to memorise, and where the rate comes from
cols: THE POSITION FOR 6 APRIL 2026 TO 5 APRIL 2027
rows: Annual exempt amount
£3,000. The same as the previous tax year, having fallen gradually from a high of £12,300. It cannot be carried forward or transferred if it goes unused.
Rate within the unused basic rate band
18% on gains up to the amount of basic rate band left after the taxpayer's taxable income has been taxed.
Rate above the unused basic rate band
24%. A higher rate income taxpayer therefore pays 24% on all their gains, subject to business asset disposal relief.
Business asset disposal relief rate
18% on qualifying gains. It was 14% in the previous tax year and 10% before that.
Business asset disposal relief lifetime limit
£1m of gains for each individual, over their lifetime.
Non-wasting chattel exemption
The gain is exempt if the disposal proceeds are £6,000 or less.
Payment date
31 January following the tax year in which the gain was made. There are no payments on account, unlike income tax.
UK residential property
The tax must be reported and paid within 60 days of completion.

visuals.label: Losses and the annual exempt amount — the ordering trap
rows: Same-year losses are set off automatically
A gain of £12,000 and a loss of £3,000 in the same year net to £9,000. The taxpayer has no choice about this.
Losses can still be steered
Where there are several gains, losses should be allocated to the gains NOT eligible for business asset disposal relief, because those carry the higher rate.
Excess losses carry forward indefinitely
If the year's losses exceed the year's gains, the chargeable gain is nil and the unused loss is carried forward without time limit. Losses brought forward can also be steered.
But the annual exempt amount is lost
If reliefs or losses leave nothing chargeable, the annual exempt amount for that year simply disappears. It cannot be carried forward or transferred.
The anti-avoidance rule on losses

A loss cannot be set against a gain if it arose from arrangements whose main purpose was to secure a tax advantage — paying less tax, obtaining a relief or deferral, or a larger repayment. The classic example is a circular transaction that leaves the taxpayer owning the same asset.

notes.head: 7.18.2 Who pays, and on what
body: Capital gains tax bites when a chargeable person makes a chargeable disposal of a chargeable asset.
Individuals, trustees and personal representatives pay capital gains tax. A company pays CORPORATION TAX on its chargeable gains instead.
A UK resident individual is chargeable on the disposal of worldwide assets.
A non-resident is generally not chargeable, even on an asset situated here. The main exception is a disposal of an interest in UK land, whether residential or commercial.

notes.head: 7.18.2.2 Disposals that are easy to miss
body: A GIFT is a disposal, and so is the disposal of only part of an asset.
The LOSS or DESTRUCTION of an asset can be a disposal, particularly where an insurance claim produces a payment.
DEATH is not an occasion of charge. The person left the asset inherits it at market value at the date of death, the probate value.
SPOUSES and CIVIL PARTNERS transfer between themselves with no charge. The recipient is deemed to acquire at the same cost as the transferor, which is what no-gain, no-loss means.

notes.head: 7.18.3 Consideration, market value and the bad bargain
body: Start with the consideration received. A property bought for £100,000 and sold for £250,000 produces a gain of £150,000.

If the asset is GIVEN away, or sold to a CONNECTED PERSON, substitute the market value. A sale to a connected person for £200,000 where the market value is £250,000 is still taxed on a gain of £150,000.

A BAD BARGAIN at arm's length is different. A sale to an unconnected third party for £200,000 is taxed on the actual gain of £100,000, because there may be a sound commercial reason such as the need for a quick sale.

notes.head: 7.18.3.1 Allowable expenditure
body: The purchase price, or the market value at acquisition if the asset was received as a gift or on a death.
Acquisition expenses, such as legal fees and stamp duty land tax.
Incidental costs of disposal, such as legal fees, valuation fees and advertising costs.

Enhancement expenditure, most commonly building costs on an extension. It must still be reflected in the state or nature of the asset at the date of disposal — if the extension has been demolished by the time of sale, its cost is not allowable.

notes.head: 7.18.6 Anti-avoidance
body: The government uses two methods: specific provisions inside the tax legislation, and the general anti-abuse rule.
The targeted anti-avoidance rule on losses is the example the SRA specification points to. A loss cannot be offset if it arose from arrangements whose main purpose was to secure a tax advantage.
A tax advantage means paying less tax or no tax, enjoying a relief or a deferral, or receiving an increased repayment.

The give-away is a circular transaction: the taxpayer sells the loss-making asset, a spouse buys an identical holding the same day, and gifts it back on a no-gain, no-loss basis, so nothing changes except the manufactured loss.

notes.head: CURRENCY
body: The 2026 manual moved every rate and threshold out of the chapter and into the separate Tax Checker, and the March 2026 business update confirms that the Tax Checker governs for 7.16 to 7.19. The figures above are from the Tax Checker of 24 July 2026, for the tax year 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027.

The old split between a lower rate for ordinary assets and a higher rate for residential property has gone. There is now one pair of rates, 18% and 24%, for all assets, and the business asset disposal relief rate has risen from 10% to 14% and now to 18%.

statutes.ref: Taxation of Chargeable Gains Act 1992, s 1
statutes.text: Capital gains tax is charged on chargeable gains accruing to a person on the disposal of assets. Companies are charged to corporation tax on their chargeable gains rather than to capital gains tax.

Business assets roll-over relief on the replacement of business assets. Where the proceeds of a qualifying business asset are reinvested in other qualifying assets within one year before or three years after the disposal, the gain is rolled into the cost of the new asset and deferred.

Incorporation relief. Where an individual transfers a business as a going concern, with the whole of its assets, to a company wholly or partly in exchange for shares, the gain is deferred by reducing the acquisition cost of those shares.

Gift hold-over relief on gifts of business assets. On a joint claim by transferor and transferee, the transferor's gain is held over and the transferee's acquisition cost is reduced by the amount of that gain.

Business asset disposal relief. Sets out the qualifying disposals, the 5% shareholding and 2-year officer or employee conditions, the 2-year trading condition, the lifetime limit on qualifying gains and the reduced rate.

Private residence relief. A gain accruing on the disposal of a dwelling house that is or has been the individual's only or main residence, together with land occupied as its garden or grounds up to the permitted area, is relieved in the proportion that the period of occupation bears to the period of ownership.

7.18.tip: ⚡ SQE: Chargeable person + chargeable disposal + chargeable asset. Gift or connected person = MARKET VALUE; bad bargain at arm's length = actual price. Death is not a disposal and the beneficiary takes probate value; spouses transfer no-gain, no-loss. Reliefs: hold-over for gifts of business assets, roll-over for reinvestment 1 year before to 3 years after, incorporation for business-into-shares, EIS for any gain reinvested in unquoted shares, private residence for the home. Business asset disposal relief is a RATE applied at the end, not a step 3 relief. 2026/27: annual exempt amount £3,000; 18% within the unused basic rate band, 24% above it; business asset disposal relief 18% up to £1m lifetime. Pay by 31 January, but UK residential property within 60 days of completion.

7.19.title: Value Added Tax

visuals.label: Mind map — the whole of 7.19

branches.label: WHEN VAT IS CHARGED
leaves: There must be a SUPPLY of goods or services, made in the UK
It must be made by a TAXABLE PERSON — someone who makes or intends to make taxable supplies and is required to be registered
It must be made while CARRYING ON A BUSINESS, which includes any trade, profession or vocation
A price is deemed to INCLUDE VAT unless it says otherwise
A person can be a company, a partnership or an LLP, and a partnership registers in the partnership's own name

branches.label: OUTPUT TAX AND INPUT TAX
leaves: OUTPUT TAX is the VAT the business charges its own customers on what it supplies
INPUT TAX is the VAT the business itself pays on what it buys
The business pays HMRC the difference, and is REIMBURSED where the input tax exceeds the output tax
The effect is that VAT is borne by the FINAL CONSUMER, not by the businesses in the chain

branches.label: REGISTRATION
leaves: COMPULSORY where taxable supplies in the previous 12 months exceed the registration threshold — a rolling test done at the end of every month
COMPULSORY also where there are reasonable grounds to believe the next 30 DAYS alone will exceed the threshold
VOLUNTARY registration is allowed below the threshold, and lets the business recover its input tax
The price of voluntary registration is that the business must charge output tax, a real cost to an unregistered customer
DEREGISTRATION is allowed once turnover falls below the deregistration threshold for 12 months, and is compulsory within 30 days of ceasing to make taxable supplies

branches.label: HOW A SUPPLY IS TREATED
leaves: STANDARD RATED at 20% — most goods and services
REDUCED RATED at 5% — domestic fuel, installation of energy-saving materials, child car seats
ZERO RATED at 0% — food other than catering, books and newspapers, water and sewerage, transport, residential construction
EXEMPT — insurance, financial services, education, and normally the sale, lease and letting of commercial land and buildings
OUTSIDE THE SCOPE — a private sale, an MOT fee, the sale of shares, and the sale of a business as a going concern

branches.label: OPTING TO TAX LAND
leaves: The sale or lease of land is normally an EXEMPT supply, so the input tax on it cannot be recovered
The owner of COMMERCIAL land or buildings may OPT TO TAX, which makes the supply standard rated and unlocks input tax recovery
The option applies to that individual building, but once made it applies to the WHOLE of it
It binds all FUTURE supplies of that property, whether sale or lease
It does NOT pass with the land: it belongs to the person who made it

visuals.label: Decision tree — can this business recover its input tax?

nodes.q: 1. What kind of supplies does the business make?

a.k: TAXABLE SUPPLIES — STANDARD OR REDUCED RATE
a.v: It charges output tax at 20% or 5%, deducts the input tax it has paid, and pays HMRC the difference.
Zero rating is still a TAXABLE supply. The business charges 0% output tax but recovers its input tax in full, so it is usually in repayment and often makes monthly claims to help cashflow.
It cannot register, and so cannot reclaim any VAT. The input tax it pays is simply a cost of doing business.

a.k: A MIXTURE OF ZERO-RATED AND EXEMPT
a.v: A partially exempt trader. Normally only a proportion of its input tax is recoverable.

nodes.q: 2. What was the purchase for?

a.v: No recovery. VAT on supplies relating to non-business activity cannot be reclaimed.
Only the business proportion is recoverable — a computer used partly at home is the standard example.
In most cases the input VAT on the purchase of a car cannot be reclaimed at all, because of the potential for personal use.
Blocked. VAT on business entertaining cannot be reclaimed.
No recovery either way. A person deducting input tax in a VAT return must hold tax invoices to back the claim up.

nodes.q: 3. The purchase is a commercial property — should the owner opt to tax?

a.v: Buying a new commercial building is a taxable transaction, so the landlord pays standard rate VAT on it. Renting it out would be an exempt supply, which makes that large input tax irrecoverable.
Opting to tax converts the letting into a taxable supply, so the input tax on the purchase price becomes recoverable, along with inputs on heating, cleaning and repairs.
Standard rate VAT must then be charged on the premium and the rents. That hurts a tenant who makes wholly or partly exempt supplies, because they cannot recover it.

a.k: AND IT IS HARD TO UNDO
a.v: HMRC will revoke the option within 6 MONTHS if the owner changes their mind and has not yet acted on it, for example by charging rent inclusive of VAT. Otherwise it can only be revoked after 20 YEARS, with HMRC's consent.
